subject: science
domain: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions
skillName: Gravity Pulls Objects Down Toward Earth
intro: Earth pulls on every object with a force called gravity. This force always points down, toward the center of the Earth. That is why a dropped ball falls to the ground, why things have weight, and why water pours downward. No matter where you stand on Earth, down means toward the center of the planet, so people on opposite sides of the globe both have their feet pointing toward the center. Gravity is what keeps objects, and us, on the ground.

items.prompt: A student lets go of a ball above the floor. Which way does it move, and what force causes this?

steps: Earth exerts a force of gravity on the ball.
Gravity always pulls objects down, toward the center of the Earth.
So the released ball falls straight down to the floor.
solution.answer: It falls down, because Earth's gravity pulls it toward the center of the planet.

items.prompt: A person in the United States and a person in Australia are on nearly opposite sides of the globe. For each person, which direction is down?

steps: Down means the direction gravity pulls, which is toward the center of the Earth.
For the person in the United States, toward the center is one direction; for the person in Australia, toward the center is the opposite direction in space.
Yet both feel their own 'down' as toward Earth's center, which is why both stay on the ground.
solution.answer: For both people, down is toward the center of the Earth, even though those are opposite directions in space.

items.prompt: Why does a book resting on a table have weight?

steps: Weight is a measure of the pull of gravity on an object.
Earth's gravity pulls the book down toward the center of the planet.
This downward pull is what we measure as the book's weight.
solution.answer: Because Earth's gravity pulls the book down, and that pull is its weight.

items.prompt: Water poured from a pitcher always falls downward. What force explains this?

steps: Gravity pulls all matter, including water, toward Earth's center.
So the water falls down when it leaves the pitcher.
solution.answer: Gravity, which pulls the water down toward the center of the Earth.

items.prompt: A student throws a ball straight up. Explain why it slows, stops, and comes back down.

steps: Gravity always pulls the ball down toward Earth's center.
On the way up, gravity acts against the motion and slows the ball until it stops.
Then gravity keeps pulling it down, so the ball falls back to the ground.
solution.answer: Gravity pulls it down the whole time, so the ball slows, stops, and then falls back down.

items.prompt: A feather and a rock are both dropped. Ignoring air, which way does gravity pull each one, and toward what point?

steps: Gravity pulls on all objects, both the feather and the rock.
The pull is downward for each object, toward the center of the Earth.
solution.answer: Gravity pulls both of them down, toward the center of the Earth.
